topic: Space-Filling Curves: Bridging the Finite and the Infinite
target_audience: University students (STEM majors) or advanced high school students

sections.title: The Paradox of Dimensionality (0:00-0:45)
animations: Create a 2D plane labeled "Space" (#FFFFFF) and a 1D line labeled "Data" (#FFFF00).
Highlight the 2D plane expanding in all directions.
Show the 1D line trying to fill the 2D space.
Demonstrate how the 1D line gets closer to covering the area.

sections.title: Constructing the Peano Curve (0:45-2:00)
lecture_lines: We start with a simple cross.
animations: Display a square unit area with 0 to 1 axes.
Draw the first iteration of the Peano curve connecting points.
Transition to the second iteration showing increased complexity.
Show the third iteration highlighting the self-similar pattern emerging.
Finalize with the limit curve filling the interior of the square.

sections.title: The Infinite Limit: Breaking Topology (2:00-3:30)
lecture_lines: The curve becomes a continuous function.
animations: Display a continuous line mapping from [0, 1] to [0, 1]x[0, 1].
Show the curve breaking the traditional concept of dimension.
Animate the transformation showing points getting closer together.
Highlight the divergence between the curve's path and its topology.
Conclude with the paradox showing a 1D object filling 2D space.

sections.title: Real-World Applications (3:30-4:30)
animations: Display an image processing icon representing data mapping.
Animate the curve traversing through a grid of pixels.
